summary: Latency regression after enabling new optimization config (batching/caching) on Dedicated us-east
description:
Customer reports a latency regression immediately after enabling a new Optimization Config setting (batching heuristic update + KV prefix cache toggle) on their Dedicated deployment in us-east.

Issue summary
- Dedicated deployment: northbridge-analytics / deployment `nb-prod-dedicated-us-east-1`
- Model: llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Change applied: Optimization Config version `ocfg_2025-12-18_03` (previous: `ocfg_2025-12-10_02`)
- Symptoms: p95 latency increased ~3x, queueing/TTFT increase, customer impact on synchronous endpoints
- Immediate mitigation: rollback to prior Optimization Config version (confirmed recovery)

Customer impact
- Impact window: 2025-12-18 16:22–17:05 UTC (approx)
- p95 latency: ~0.9–1.1s baseline -> 2.6–3.2s after change
- p99 latency: ~2.8–3.5s baseline -> 6.5–7.8s after change
- Error rate: no material change (customer reports <0.3% 5xx)
- Business impact: degraded UX for their "insights" feature; customer paused planned rollout

Environment / routing
- Region: us-east
- Dedicated cluster: `dedicated-us-east-1-gpu-pool-3`
- Customer observed response header: `x-redwood-opt-config-version: ocfg_2025-12-18_03` on impacted requests

What changed (per customer + internal notes)
- Enabled: `batching.heuristic = "adaptive_v3"` (more aggressive continuous batching at moderate concurrency)
- Enabled: `cache.kv_prefix_cache = true` with `cache.max_prefix_bytes` increased for long-prompt workloads

Steps to reproduce (from customer)
1) Send a batch of ~50 concurrent chat completion requests with prompt lengths ~4k–10k tokens.
2) Compare p95 / p99 latency before and after enabling the new optimization config.
3) Regression appears within minutes; mostly increased time-to-first-token and end-to-end latency.

Examples
- Request IDs (customer provided):
  - `req_01HF7N2K9E9YH3WZP0F4C0Q1X7`
  - `req_01HF7N3A2V2W0Z7T5B8K7T1M9P`
  - `req_01HF7N4J8GZP2K3D1Q8W9N0R6S`

Initial hypothesis
- New batching heuristic increased batch residency time under sustained concurrency (goodput improved but tail latency worsened).
- KV prefix cache setting increased GPU memory pressure, causing intermittent eviction/churn and scheduler backpressure.

Mitigation taken
- Rolled back Optimization Config to `ocfg_2025-12-10_02` for tenant northbridge-analytics in us-east.
- Customer confirmed latency returned to baseline within ~10 minutes post-rollback.

Follow-ups
- Identify whether regression is workload-specific (long prompts + high concurrency) and whether we need per-tenant overrides.
- Add gating for p95/p99 latency and GPU memory saturation metrics prior to promotion of aggressive batching/caching configs.
- Ensure audit log export includes rollback event (customer asked for change traceability).
